punchline: A zebra relaxes when the lion leaves, but a human can keep the same alarm running with a single thought.
thirty_sec: Robert Sapolsky opens with a zebra fleeing a lion: its heart races, its muscles get energy, its digestion stops. Once it escapes, it calms down and goes back to grazing. People trigger the same response with thoughts about rent or exams, and those thoughts can last for days. The difference lies in whether the alarm ever switches off.
